newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa's Mandela steps into Great Lakes crisis.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Mandela steps into Great Lakes crisis.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela will attend a one-day summit in Nairobi on Monday on the Great Lakes crisis, his spokesman said on Saturday.

It is the first time Mandela, seen by many Africans as the best hope for their continent, has played a direct role in efforts to resolve a crisis that began in Rwanda and has spread fighting and refugees across Central Africa.

"The president is definitely going," Mandela's spokesman Parks Mankahlana told Reuters. "He was invited and decided to go because he is concerned about the situation, and reports yesterday that it may be getting worse."

Other regional leaders are due to attend the summit in the Kenyan capital to address spreading fighting in Zaire and the plight of Rwandan and Burundian Hutu refugees on the move there and in Tanzania.

Mandela said in October he would send troops to a planned multinational force to bring aid to hundreds of thousands of refugees in eastern Zaire. The plans were put on ice after many refugees returned home to Rwanda last month, and a Canadian spokesman said on Saturday the mission had been formally closed.
